title: Futures Slide as Alphabet Sinks on Results, Nasdaq Leads a Pre-Bell Pullback
dek: Nasdaq 100 futures fell about 1% before the open as Alphabet's revenue miss and free-cash-flow worries hit the megacaps, while Microsoft traded higher after its beat.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Federal Reserve Building in Washington, D.C.

keyPoints: Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1.1% and S&P 500 futures about 0.3% at 8:02 AM ET, per Investopedia, after the Fed held rates on a 10-2 vote on Wednesday.
Alphabet fell about 11% in premarket trading after results that Yahoo Finance said missed on revenue; cloud growth was reported at 103%, but free-cash-flow and AI-return concerns weighed.
Microsoft rose about 1.5% premarket after beating expectations on the top and bottom lines, with cloud demand cited as the driver.
The 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.03% and WTI crude near $102 a barrel; CME FedWatch implied about 84% odds of a December rate increase, per Investopedia.
body:
U.S. stock futures split before the open on Thursday. Nasdaq 100 futures fell about 1.1% in recent trading, while S&P 500 futures were down about 0.3% and Dow futures fell 0.3%, according to Investopedia. Yahoo Finance's early-session live feed showed Dow futures up 0.3%, so the Dow picture is mixed and the early numbers are volatile.

The drag came from Alphabet. Its shares were pointing roughly 11% lower before the bell after the company reported third-quarter results that Yahoo Finance said came in short on sales. Yahoo also noted that cloud growth of 103% was not enough to offset investor concern about free cash flow and the return on AI spending. Before the release, market-makers had priced a move of about 5.8% in Alphabet stock, per Cboe LiveVol data cited by CNBC.

Microsoft moved the other way. Its shares were up about 1.5% in premarket trading after results that beat expectations, with Yahoo Finance pointing to cloud demand as the main support. The split sharpened a broader question for the megacaps: which AI spending is being rewarded and which is being questioned.

Semiconductors and AI hardware also came under pressure. Yahoo Finance reported that the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) fell more than 2% and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) fell more than 3% on Thursday. Samsung Electronics ended 4% lower in Seoul, per Investopedia.

The Fed backdrop remains the frame. Policymakers held the benchmark rate in a 3.75% to 4% range on a 10-2 vote, with Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Governor Lisa Cook dissenting in favor of a hike. Traders still priced a December increase as likely, with CME FedWatch implying about 84% odds per Investopedia. A 10-year yield near 5.03% keeps pressure on long-duration assets.

What to watch at 8:30 AM ET: the advance estimate of third-quarter GDP and September personal income and outlays, which the Bureau of Economic Analysis lists for Thursday. Amazon reports after the close.

marketImpact.summary: Futures point to a softer open led by megacap tech. Alphabet's drop is the main near-term risk to the Nasdaq; Microsoft's gain and the hawkish rate backdrop make the reaction uneven rather than a broad sell-off.
marketImpact.timeframe: Thursday's open through the 8:30 AM ET data and Amazon's results

tickers.rationale: Premarket decline of about 11% after results that missed on revenue and raised free-cash-flow concerns.
Premarket gain of about 1.5% after a beat on the top and bottom lines.
Semiconductor ETF fell more than 2% as AI hardware names weakened.
10-year yield near 5.03% with a December hike priced at roughly 84%.

Amazon quarterly results after the close
